lessonRef.unitTitle: PF3 — Budgeting and Saving: Multi-Year Planning, Inflation, and Goal Conflict
lessonRef.title: Applied simulation: behavioural pressures on a savings plan

focus: behavioural pressures on a savings plan
objective: Quantify the gap between a fictional intended savings rate and the amount actually saved, add a recurring leak, and express the five-year cost of the difference between a plan and a habit.
scenario: Freya Okoro-Villalobos is a fictional saver whose simulated records are summarised below. The intended amounts, the actual amounts, and the subscriptions are invented figures.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional savings record in these directions

tasks.directions: Freya intends to save $400 a month by moving money manually at the end of each month. Over the past year she has actually saved an average of $215 a month. Separately she pays $87 a month across 6 subscriptions, of which 3 worth $41 a month have gone unused for the whole year.

prompts.text: What is the monthly gap between what Freya intends to save and what she actually saves?
Across 5 years, or 60 months, what does that monthly gap come to?
Across the same 60 months, what do the unused subscriptions come to?
What do the two together cost across the 5 years?

tasks.directions: Now look at what fixing each would be worth.

prompts.text: The unused subscriptions are what percentage of the $87 subscription bill? Give one decimal place.
If Freya automated the transfer and cancelled the unused subscriptions, how much more would she have each month?
What percentage of her $400 target would the recovered amount represent? Give one decimal place.
Which change would do more over the 5 years?
choices: Automating the transfer so the intended $400 is actually saved
They are worth the same amount

tasks.directions: Answer each in a few sentences.

prompts.text: Freya’s plan is arithmetically sound and she is $13,560.00 behind it over five years. Explain what kind of failure that is, and describe one change to the design of the plan — not to her willpower — that would close most of the gap.

Cancelling the subscriptions is worth $2,460.00 and takes an afternoon; automating the transfer is worth $11,100.00 and takes minutes. Say why someone might still do the first and not the second, and what that suggests about ordering changes to a plan.

remediation: If the recovered monthly amount comes out at $185.00, the subscriptions have been left out; if it comes out at $272.00, the whole $87 subscription bill is being counted rather than the $41 that goes unused. Freya still uses three of the six services, so only $41 is recoverable. Write the two recoverable lines separately and check each against the scenario before adding.
extension: Work out how many months of the automated $400 it would take to reach $13,560.00, and say what that period represents in terms of the plan Freya already has.
